evidence.dominant_driver: Von der Leyen says EU-China trade deficit reached a tipping point and EU will use all available trade tools; no concrete tariff action announced yet.

absorption.reason: No reliable instrument-specific reaction since 07:27 UTC was available by decision time; broader European equities had been rebounding before the headline.

observations.oil: WTI/Brent pulling back but still elevated
observations.rates: US10Y and Bund yields easing from peaks
observations.fed: Fed hike ~93% priced for later today

evidence.decision_notes: Fresh policy rhetoric, but residual forecast is from 08:01 UTC and avoids assuming the original headline reaction. Learning profile had no ACTIONABLE M2 evidence segment applicable enough to alter confidence.

immediate.rationale: Fresh rhetoric but no immediate tariff measure; Fed/oil relief dominate current tape.

next_session.rationale: Policy follow-through is needed for a durable index effect.

15m.rationale: No enacted measure and European equities were already rebounding.

1h.rationale: Trade friction is a headwind but falling oil/yields offset it.

4h.rationale: Fed decision later today is likely to dominate.

next_session.rationale: Direction depends on concrete EU measures or Chinese retaliation.

predictions.mechanism: Potential EU-China trade escalation can pressure China-exposed exporters and industrials.
predictions.invalidation: No concrete trade action and continued equity rebound despite the rhetoric.
predictions.counter_case: Markets treat the speech as negotiating rhetoric; lower oil/yields and Fed relief extend the European rebound.

technical_state.source: pre-decision Reuters market context; exact post-headline instrument reaction unavailable
